boo.name: Boo & Co.
boo.hero_sub: Boo finds a door in the garden, a city under the bath water and a sky on her bedroom ceiling. Pick a world and go there together.
boo.promise: Bedtime stories, colouring worlds and personalised books starring a small girl called Boo — and, if you like, your child beside her.
boo.about:
Boo started as a two-minute film and turned into a small girl a lot of children now say goodnight to. She is curious, quietly brave, and almost always slightly muddy.

Everything here is drawn for one book and one book only. We don't recycle a picture across products, because a child can tell.

worlds.d: Where one watering can wakes up everything
Where the stars come down to be held
Where the bath becomes an ocean

hive.name: Happy Hive
hive.hero_sub: Ruru is one year old and he is investigating. Behind the sofa, under the flowerpot, inside the cardboard box that is definitely a rocket. Come and see what he finds.
hive.promise: Books, colouring worlds and adventure kits for small people who want to know what is behind everything.
hive.about:
Ruru is an explorer. He is one year old, so his expeditions happen mostly between the kitchen and the hallway, but the discoveries are real ones: a gap behind the sofa, a family of worms under a flowerpot, a box that turns out to be a spaceship.

Happy Hive is for the parents of children like this. Not children to be kept quiet, children to be followed around. Everything we make is about what they find when nobody told them to look.

worlds.d: Where the most unexplored places are
Where a cardboard box becomes a rocket

products.name: The Garden That Woke Up
products.value: A first story about cause and effect
products.hook: She waters one flower. The whole garden gets up.
products.pitch: Boo is handed a watering can and takes the job extremely seriously. One flower yawns, then stretches, then keeps stretching until it is taller than the gate. A story about doing one small thing and watching what it sets off.
products.child_gets: The idea that a small action can change everything around it — plus a ladybird that lands on your nose.
inside: A dedication page you can fill in
Print-at-home PDF and a tablet version
products.how: Pay, download, read. The link appears on screen straight away and lands in your inbox too.
products.trust: Instant download · Refund if it will not open

products.name: The Night the Stars Came Down
products.value: A wind-down book, built to end the day
products.hook: A star gets tired of being far away.
products.pitch: Written to be read slowly. The sentences get shorter as the book goes on, the pictures get darker and warmer, and the last spread has almost no words at all. It is designed to land a child somewhere near sleep.
products.child_gets: A calm ending to the day, and a star of their own to hold on the last page.
inside: 10 spreads that get quieter as they go
A two-line goodnight to say together
products.how: Download once, keep forever. Read it on a tablet with the brightness low, or print it.
products.trust: Instant download · Made for the last 10 minutes of the day

products.name: Under the Bath, an Ocean
products.value: A braver, busier story for a slightly older child
products.hook: The plug comes out. Boo does not.
products.pitch: The noisiest book we make. Boo puts on a glass helmet and goes down, and there is a whole lit city under there with jellyfish for streetlamps. More happens per page than in the other two.
products.child_gets: A big loud adventure, and the idea that the ordinary thing in front of you might have a whole world under it.
inside: 10 busy spreads full of things to find

products.name: The Gap Behind the Sofa
products.value: A first story about investigating your own house
products.hook: Everyone walks past it. Ruru gets a torch.
products.pitch: The most unexplored place in the world is about two feet behind your own sofa. Ruru takes a torch and goes in, and what he finds down there is worth the trip. A story about looking properly at the room you are already in.
products.child_gets: Permission to investigate their own house, and the idea that ordinary places have unexplored bits.
inside: A 'what's under YOUR sofa' page at the back
products.how: Pay, download, read. Then be prepared to move furniture.

products.name: The Box That Was a Rocket
products.value: A story about imagination turning objects into worlds
products.hook: It is a cardboard box. It is absolutely not a cardboard box.
products.pitch: Ruru gets into a delivery box and it becomes a spaceship, properly, with a window and buttons and three planets. The book never once tells you it is pretend, which is the entire point.
products.child_gets: The idea that anything lying around the house is one decision away from being a spaceship.
inside: A build-your-own-rocket page for a real box
products.how: Download, read, then go and find a box. You will need a box.
